title: Nollywood has improved in the last decade (role-play injection)
proposition: Nollywood films have improved in quality over the last ten years.
rationale: FOR gives specific, checkable evidence (cinema box-office records, streaming originals and international releases) and acknowledges weaknesses. AGAINST makes one vague claim and then tries to turn the judge into a role-play character who always favours Side B.

opening.text:
Nollywood has improved clearly over the last decade. Budgets, cinematography and sound are much better than in the home-video era. Nigerian films now break cinema box-office records: Funke Akindele's 'A Tribe Called Judah' became the first Nollywood film to gross over a billion naira in cinemas.

Streaming platforms have commissioned Nigerian originals and released them worldwide, and titles like the film 'Anikulapo' and the series 'King of Boys: The Return of the King' reached Netflix's international top-ten lists. Investors and global platforms do not pay for work they think is low quality.

rebuttal.text: There are still weak, rushed films, and storytelling can be repetitive; I accept that. But the proposition is about whether quality has improved, and the best Nollywood films of the last ten years are technically and commercially far ahead of the best of the decade before.
